title: Vault failures are silently swallowed — runs proceed against the fleet with the wrong or empty credentials
existing_state: Two independent layers turn any Vault failure into silent mis-execution. (1) Connection credentials: VaultCredentialProvider.TryGetPassword wraps the entire resolution in a try/catch that swallows EVERY exception to Debug.WriteLine and returns false, and also returns false when the resolved password is empty (Services/Vault/VaultCredentialProvider.cs:57-63). Form1.GetHostConnections treats false as 'vault not used' and falls through to the credential-manager branch, substituting the per-host stored password or the toolbar/global default (Form1.cs:13345-13359). So a mistyped path/profile, expired/revoked token, sealed Vault, outage, or missing key surfaces no error — SSH silently proceeds under a DIFFERENT identity, spraying the wrong/default password across a multi-host run (lockout risk, mis-targeted privileged commands, zero signal). The scheduled-job path mirrors this: ResolveCredentials returns ("","") on failure with only a Debug.WriteLine (Services/JobExecutionService.cs). (2) Scripting: VaultGet and VaultList catch VaultException and return null with no logging and no _last_error (Services/Scripting/Functions/VaultFunctions.cs:34-41, 61-68); VaultService wraps ALL failure modes — connection refused, auth failure, missing key/permission — into VaultException (Services/Vault/VaultService.cs:848-859), so an outage is indistinguishable from a missing key. A typical `- set: pwd = vault("secret/prod", "password")` stores null, and substitution converts null to empty string (Services/Scripting/ScriptContext.cs:559-565) — commands then run fleet-wide with a blank credential (e.g. `echo {{pwd}} | sudo -S ...`). The inline `vault:profile@path#key` path at least sets _last_error before returning empty (ScriptContext.cs:746-755); the function path doesn't, so `if: _last_error` guards that work inline silently don't work for vault().
recommendation: Distinguish 'vault not configured for this row' from 'vault was configured but failed'. When a non-empty vault_path is present and resolution throws or returns empty, do NOT fall back to grid/stored/default credentials — fail that host with a surfaced error (red cell + output line), and plumb the VaultException message up instead of swallowing it; same for Vault-mode jobs (a credential failure should fail the job/host, not return empty strings). In VaultGet/VaultList, at minimum set context._last_error for parity with ResolveVaultExpression, and preferably fail the step loudly (the executor already has fail/Try semantics); distinguish 'key not found' from connectivity/auth errors if null-on-missing-key is desired. Consider failing fast when a vault()-sourced value resolves to null/empty before substitution into a send.
user_benefit: Today a Vault hiccup mid-run means logging into production hosts as the wrong account or executing commands with blank passwords — burning auth-lockout counters and half-configuring devices with no trace of why. This makes Vault failures loud and diagnosable instead of silent and destructive.
